diagram_math_checks.details: F_{n,k} is explicitly the statement’s set of framed cobordism classes of closed framed (n−k)-submanifolds of S^n, for n≥k≥1. The right node is π_n(S^k). The upper arrow Φ has domain F_{n,k} and codomain π_n(S^k); the lower Ψ has the reverse domain/codomain, exactly as proof steps 1.1 and 1.2.

The upper arrow sends [(N,φ)] to the class of the restriction f_(N,φ)|S^n using F7’s free-to-based identification, expressly stated in Remarks. This respects the disjoint-basepoint distinction in step 1.1 and def-pontryagin-thom-map-of-a-framed-submanifold rather than asserting that restriction is literally based.

The lower arrow uses a smooth representative f′, regular y and positive basis b at y, and sends [f] to [(f′⁻¹(y),f′_*b)]. def-framed-regular-preimage-of-a-map-to-a-sphere defines f′_*b via the normal-quotient derivative and basis. F3–F5 and step 1.2 establish existence and choice independence.

Ψ∘Φ=id on F_{n,k} follows from step 2.1/F6: the normalized collapse centre preimage and framing equal (N,φ) literally. Φ∘Ψ=id on π_n(S^k) follows from step 2.2/F6: the collapse of the chosen framed preimage is homotopic to f′ and hence f. The suppliers lem-regular-preimage-after-collapse-recovers-the-original-framed-submanifold and lem-collapse-after-regular-preimage-is-homotopic-to-the-original-map were read locally to verify these exact interfaces.

No nonempty fibre is drawn or assumed. Remarks explicitly retain empty fibres and n=k; the latter gives zero-dimensional framed preimages. No k=0 assertion is added. The original statement, Facts and all five proof steps are byte-preserved, and the rigorous proof does not rely on the figure.
